answer: Divergent-Challenge Liveness Proof. Each identity must periodically answer a fresh random challenge whose correct reply depends on its full interaction history, so clones sharing one history all produce the same cipher. An operator needing N distinct identities must run N genuinely divergent histories, each incurring separate compute and storage in an isolated lagoon of state. Colluding copies that diverge break synchronization and must then be maintained as independent agents across a hostile tundra of cold-start verification, paying full per-identity replay costs.
